title: Admin attack-path mitigation and RBACv2 + SSO audit closure
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: Close outstanding items from the external pentest (report PT-2026-03) and internal threat models related to RBACv2 migration, admin control planes, audit log fidelity, and SSO/SAML assertions. Scope: review and remediate attack paths that allow privilege escalation via role mapping, stale audit forwarding rules, weak SAML assertion replay protections, and unprotected admin session endpoints. Deliverables: (1) code and config fixes merged, (2) updated threat model and mitigation matrix, (3) automated audit-forwarding tests, (4) SSO regression test-suite added to CI, (5) rollout plan with canary and rollback, (6) final verification and pen-test recheck ticket closure. Out of scope: full RBAC UI redesign and third-party IdP migrations (handled in separate PM tickets).
acceptance_criteria: All high and critical findings from PT-2026-03 addressed or have compensating controls and documented residual risk
RBACv2 role mappings default to deny and explicit allow for admin scopes by attribute-based checks
Audit pipeline (log ingestion → retention → forwarding) shows no gaps: missing events are false-positive free for production window
SAML assertion replay protections (audience, AuthnInstant bounds, OneTimeUse enforcement) validated with unit/integration tests
Admin API endpoints require elevated session protection and enforced MFA for interactive sessions
Changes deployed via canary to limited orgs and metrics show no increase in 5xx or auth-failures before global rollout
tasks: Threat model update: enumerate attack trees for admin elevation and cross-tenant impersonation
Fix 3 RBAC mapping rules that implicitly granted admin via legacy role aliases
Add attribute-based checks (org_role + org_id + session_nonce) to admin token validation path
Patch SAML verifier to enforce OneTimeUse and tighten clock skew acceptance to 90s for high-risk flows
Hardening: require session binding and rotate admin session cookie name and flags
Audit pipeline: add event ids for role-change events and instrument forwarder to drop events with malformed context
End-to-end tests: add SSO replay simulation, role-change audit verification, and admin endpoint MFA smoke tests
Prepare PRs, link to confluence design, and create canary runbook for ops
remediation_steps: ENG-93321-PR1: rbac-service: change default role resolution to explicit deny; remove legacy alias mapping (diff: github.com/redwood/rbac/PR/462)
ENG-93321-PR2: auth-service: enforce attribute-based policy evaluation for admin scopes (PR 468)
ENG-93321-PR3: saml-verifier: add OneTimeUse cache and reduce allowed_clock_skew to 90s (PR 471)
ENG-93321-PR4: audit-forwarder: validate event.context.organization_id and drop malformed events (PR 473)
Config: add runtime flag --admin-session-mfa-enforce=true and secure cookie name RED_ADMIN_SES to prod deploy config
Ops: add playbook step to rotate legacy admin API keys and revoke sessions older than 30 days
test_plan: Unit: new tests for role resolution edge cases, SAML OneTimeUse enforcement, and audit forwarder drop logic
Integration: CI pipeline job 'security/sso-rbac-regressions' runs SAML replay and role-change flow against a staging IdP
E2E Canary: deploy to 5 internal orgs, run synthetic admin actions, assert audit events in ELK and retention/forwarding success
Pen-test validation: request re-run of PT-2026-03 high-critical cases after rollout and attach re-test report to ticket
risk_assessment: High: several privilege-escalation vectors were identified that could allow cross-tenant access or persistent admin session hijack. Likelihood rated medium due to exploit complexity; impact rated high because admin actions can modify user data and billing. Residual risk accepted only with MFA-enforced admin sessions and strict audit trails.
decisions: Adopt attribute-based policy evaluation for admin authorization rather than permissive role aliases
Keep clock skew tight for high-risk SSO flows (90s) and document IdP requirements in SSO onboarding guide
Treat audit-forwarder failures as paged incidents at critical severity and block automated removal of events without manual review
Require security review sign-off for any future RBAC rule that grants write or admin scopes

2026-03-02 SR (Security): Requested addition of OneTimeUse enforcement and a replay-cache design doc. Marked two items as critical for customer-impact.
2026-03-06 LO: Replay cache implemented with in-memory + redis backing; integration tests passing against staging IdP.
2026-03-09 QA: Canary harness prepared; added audit assertions to synthetic test suite. Found missing org_id on some historical events; created follow-up cleanup job ENG-93700.
2026-03-11 AM: Security review scheduled for 2026-03-12. Ops runbook drafted and shared with SRE for sign-off.
2026-03-12 SR: Security review complete — minor comments on telemetry naming; approved for canary rollout pending telemetry updates (addressed in PR 473).
qa_checklist: Run canary plan against internal orgs and confirm zero increase in auth-failure rate
Confirm audit-forwarder logs show role-change events with correct organization_id and user_id fields
Ensure SAML replay simulation fails as expected and is logged as security event
Validate admin session revocation and key-rotation playbook steps execute correctly in staging
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Deploy to staging and 5 internal orgs for 48 hours. Monitor auth metrics and audit event success rates.
Phase 2 (limited production): Gradual ramp to 10% of production orgs over 72 hours, blocklist any org with abnormal auth failures.
Phase 3 (full): Global rollout with ops on-call present; publish post-deploy incident runbook and update SSO onboarding docs
Rollback: revert platform flag --admin-session-mfa-enforce and re-deploy prior RBAC mapping if severe regressions observed
